question: What causes standard cramping pain after an abortion?

options.A: Buildup of gas inalos the large intestine
options.C: Stretching of the abdominal wall skin

explanation: You've got this! The uterus naturally squeezes to return to its normal size after a procedure, and those muscular contractions cause period-like cramps. Totally normal part of healing! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h1)

question: Why do patients often feel sharp pressure in the lower belly right after an abortion?

options.A: Mechanical stretching and manipulation of the cervix
options.B: Swelling of the kidneys from retained fluid
options.C: Complete blockage of the Fallopian tubes
options.D: Rapid drop in systemic blood pressure levels

explanation: Opening the cervix during the procedure stretches local tissues, which leads to some sharp pressure or cramping right after. Great clinical insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h1)

question: What is a key sign that a post-abortion patient might be in severe pain?

options.A: Drop in body temperature below normal
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin sclera
options.C: Increased heart rate and breathing rate
options.D: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: When someone is in acute pain, their body's natural fight-or-flight response kicks in, causing their heart rate and breathing to speed up. Brilliant nursing observation! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h2)

question: A nurse gives a patient pain medication. What is the best next step?

options.A: Instructing the patient to stop pressing the call bell
options.B: Documenting that the pain is completely gone forever
options.C: Reassessing the patient's pain level after a short interval
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to save hospital beds

explanation: Always close the loop! Checking back in lets you know if the drug is actually doing its job or if the patient needs extra help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h2)

question: Which type of medication is usually the first choice for treating post-abortion cramps?
explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen block prostaglandins, making them absolute superstars for tackling uterine cramps. Well done! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: Why are strong opioid painkillers usually avoided for routine home care after an abortion?

options.A: They carry high risks of sedation, nausea, and dependency
options.B: They permanently damage the lining of the stomach
options.C: They cause the uterus to stop contracting completely
options.D: They raise blood pressure to dangerously high levels

explanation: Routine cramps can usually be handled safely with milder drugs, sparing the patient from heavy side effects like sleepiness and nausea. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: How does putting a heating pad on the lower belly help with post-abortion cramps?

options.A: It stops all vaginal bleeding instantly
options.B: It numbs the skin nerves permanently
options.C: It relaxes the uterine and pelvic muscles
options.D: It lowers the body temperature safely

explanation: Warmth boosts blood flow and helps tense muscles unwind, taking the sharp edge off those cramps. Simple and effective nursing comfort care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: What is a major plus of using comfort measures (like heat or rest) alongside medicines?

options.A: They guarantee the patient will have zero bleeding
options.B: They help reduce the overall need for heavy pain medications
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for any vital sign checks
options.D: They cure underlying infections without antibiotics

explanation: Combining simple comfort tricks with meds gives wonderful relief while keeping heavy drug use to a minimum. You're thinking like a holistic nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: Which symptom suggests a patient's pain is from retained tissue rather than normal recovery?

options.A: Temporary loss of appetite for a few hours
options.B: Mild lower back ache that goes away with rest
options.C: Itchy skin rash on the arms and chest
options.D: Severe cramping accompanied by heavy bleeding or large clots

explanation: If tissue is left behind, the uterus squeezes extra hard to push it out, causing intense cramps and heavy bleeding. Always watch out for this red flag! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of post-abortion recovery?

options.A: Mild intermittent cramping similar to menstrual periods
options.B: Severe lower abdominal pain that worsens over time
options.C: Light spotting that gradually decreases over days
options.D: Occasional mild fatigue following the procedure

explanation: Pain that keeps getting worse instead of better is a warning sign that something needs medical attention. Great job spotting the abnormal finding! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h5)

question: Why should a nurse give written discharge instructions about pain meds to a recovering patient?

options.A: It replaces the need for any verbal conversation entirely
options.B: Written papers are legally required to keep nurses from being sued
options.C: Patients often forget verbal instructions due to stress and fatigue
options.D: Pharmacies will not sell pain medication without hospital paper

explanation: When people are stressed or tired, details slip their minds. Written guides are lifesavers for safe home care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)

question: A patient getting ready for discharge is worried about taking her pain pills right. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient not to worry because pain is all in the mind
options.B: Cancel the prescription and give only herbal remedies instead
options.C: Ask a family member to manage all medication doses at home
options.D: Review the medication schedule slowly and check for understanding

explanation: Taking a little extra time to walk through the dosing schedule ensures the patient feels confident and safe at home. Excellent patient advocacy! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)
